prompt: A candle starts $20$ cm tall and burns $2$ cm every hour. Write an equation for its height $h$ after $t$ hours.
hint: The candle gets shorter as time passes. What does that mean for the sign of the rate of change?

hints.text: The candle gets shorter as time passes. What does that mean for the sign of the rate of change?
The starting height is $20$ and the candle loses $2$ cm each hour, so subtract $2t$ from $20$.
Starting at $20$ and losing $2$ per hour gives the equation $h = 20 - 2t$.

explanation: At $t = 0$ the candle is $20$ cm tall, so the starting value is $20$.
The candle loses $2$ cm every hour, so the rate of change is negative: $m = -2$.
Starting value plus rate times hours gives the equation $h = 20 - 2t$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check an hour
steps: After $3$ hours the candle burned $3 \times 2 = 6$ cm, leaving $20 - 6 = 14$ cm.

alternativeExplanations.title: Downhill stairs table
steps: Hour $0 \to 20$, hour $1 \to 18$, hour $2 \to 16$: a steady jump of $-2$.
Jump $-2$ is the slope, start $20$ is $b$: $h = -2t + 20$, the same as $20 - 2t$.
